name: Controlled-substance dispenses audited
definition: Share of controlled-substance dispenses screened by an automated rule or reviewed by a person in the period.
numerator: Dispense transactions screened by at least one rule or reviewed by hand
denominator: All controlled-substance dispense transactions in the period
starting_target: Every dispense rule-screened, plus a documented sample reviewed by hand (sample size is a local risk decision)
notes: A feed that silently drops a cabinet or unit lowers this number; reconcile transaction counts against the source system.

name: Discrepancy rate
definition: Count discrepancies per 1,000 doses by unit, plus the share resolved within the policy window.
numerator: Count discrepancies in the period (report resolved-in-window separately)
denominator: Doses dispensed in the period, divided by 1,000
frequency: Weekly by unit; monthly on the scorecard
starting_target: Each unit at or below its own trailing 90-day baseline
notes: Do not compare units of different size on raw counts. A new cabinet or changed counting rule shifts the baseline.

name: Median days from signal to case closure
definition: Median calendar days from the first alert on a person or event to a recorded outcome.
numerator: Median of (closure date minus first-alert date) across cases closed in the period
denominator: Cases closed in the period (report n beside the median)
starting_target: Local figure for ordinary alerts and a separate local figure for formal investigations
notes: Report ordinary alerts and formal investigations separately. Also show the age of cases still open.

name: Waste doses witnessed
definition: Waste events with a valid, contemporaneous witness divided by all waste events.
numerator: Waste events with a valid, contemporaneous witness
denominator: All waste events in the period
frequency: Weekly by unit; monthly on the scorecard
starting_target: As close to all as the process allows; every exception documented by reason
notes: Track exceptions by reason (downtime, single-nurse unit with written exception path) so they are not lumped together.

name: ADC and override compliance rate
definition: Overrides with a valid documented reason and a timely pharmacist review, divided by all overrides; plus the share of cabinet users with current access.
numerator: Overrides with a valid documented reason and pharmacist review inside the policy window
frequency: Weekly by unit; monthly on the scorecard
starting_target: Nearly all overrides reviewed within the policy window; ED and OR carry more overrides by design
notes: If the cabinet has no override reason field, count only the pharmacist-review half and record the gap as a program risk.

name: Staff training completion
definition: Share of staff with controlled-substance access who completed diversion training in the policy cycle, by role.
numerator: Staff with active access who completed training in the policy cycle
denominator: All staff with active controlled-substance access
starting_target: Near 100% of staff with access, reported by role
notes: Report by role so a gap in one group is visible. Deactivated access should leave the denominator.

name: Investigations closed with documented outcome
definition: Investigations that ended with a recorded outcome category and action, divided by investigations closed.
numerator: Closed investigations with an outcome category and an action recorded
denominator: All investigations closed in the period
starting_target: 100%; a closure with no outcome should not be possible in the case system
notes: Counts only in leadership materials. Closure requires the sign-offs listed under the monthly operating rhythm.

name: Repeat-offender detection rate
definition: Of people with two or more alerts in a rolling window (for example 90 days), the share escalated to review.
numerator: People with two or more alerts in the window who were escalated to review
denominator: People with two or more alerts in the window
notes: Numbers are small; report the counts next to the rate and never name the people on the scorecard.
